```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  echo = FALSE,
  fig.width = 7,
  fig.height = 4.5,
  dpi = 150,
  message = FALSE,
  warning = FALSE
)
library(knowledge)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
# pkgdown sets IN_PKGDOWN while it builds the website: the site gets the interactive map, the package copy the
# static one
on_site <- identical(Sys.getenv("IN_PKGDOWN"), "true")
```

```{r load}
# data from data-raw/vignette_chinook.R
vd <- function(f) system.file("vignette-data", f, package = "knowledge", mustWork = TRUE)
x <- readRDS(vd("chinook_rearing.rds"))
seg <- readRDS(vd("bulk_segments.rds"))
water <- readRDS(vd("bulk_water.rds"))
# the map group's outline, British Columbia, its towns and rivers (data-raw/vignette_context.R), for the static map
ctx <- readRDS(vd("bulk_context.rds"))
stopifnot(identical(ctx$meta$map_group, x$meta$map_group))
# the static map's canvas takes the group's shape: its outline padded 2 km, as knw_compare_map() draws it
map_bb <- sf::st_bbox(ctx$aoi)
map_h <- 6 * (map_bb[["ymax"]] - map_bb[["ymin"]] + 4000) / (map_bb[["xmax"]] - map_bb[["xmin"]] + 4000)

tune <- x$tune
summ <- x$summary
meta <- x$meta
cmp <- x$compare
dflt <- tune[tune$is_default, ]
rec <- tune[tune$recommended %in% TRUE, ]
region <- tune[tune$in_region, ]
all_row <- cmp[cmp$watershed_group_code == "ALL", ]
per_group <- cmp[cmp$watershed_group_code != "ALL", ]
map_row <- cmp[cmp$watershed_group_code == meta$map_group, ]
seeds <- x$seeds
honest <- x$honest

# formatting
n0 <- function(v) format(round(v), big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE, trim = TRUE)
n1 <- function(v) format(round(v, 1), big.mark = ",", nsmall = 1, scientific = FALSE, trim = TRUE)
pc <- function(v, d = 0) paste0(formatC(100 * v, format = "f", digits = d), " %")
grad <- function(g) paste0(signif(100 * g, 4), " %")
km_d <- function(d) if (d >= 1000) paste(format(d / 1000, trim = TRUE), "km") else paste(d, "m")
lst <- function(v, and = "and") if (length(v) < 2) v else paste(paste(v[-length(v)], collapse = ", "), and, v[length(v)])
words <- function(r) {
  size <- if (r$size_var == "mad") sprintf("an average flow of at least %s m³/s", format(r$size_min, trim = TRUE))
          else sprintf("a channel at least %s m wide", format(r$size_min, trim = TRUE))
  if (is.na(r$exc_q)) return(sprintf("a slope of at most %s, and %s", grad(r$grad_max), size))
  sprintf("a slope of at most %s, and either %s or a river of at least %s m³/s within %s downstream",
          grad(r$grad_max), size, r$exc_q, km_d(r$exc_d))
}
# every rule in the close-call set has the same shape, link's rule is outside it, and the recommended rule draws less
# habitat than link's, losing more than it gains; the sentences below say so
stopifnot(all(region$size_var == "mad"), all(!is.na(region$exc_q)), dflt$ddev_best > dflt$se_diff,
          all(region$departures == 3), is.na(dflt$exc_q), dflt$size_var == "width", all_row$change_pct < 0,
          all_row$lost_km > all_row$gained_km, all_row$gained_exception_km > 0)

# catch rates at the electrofishing sites in the groups the comparison ran; the checks table names each structure the
# comparison ran (#73), and the recommended rule's row is the tuned structure's
fv <- x$checks[x$checks$check == "fdis_visits", ]
tuned_as <- meta$tuned_structure
rate <- function(r, s) {
  v <- fv[fv$rule == r & fv$segment == s, ]
  stopifnot(nrow(v) == 1)
  v$n_detect / v$n
}
stopifnot(tuned_as %in% fv$rule)
r_rec_in <- rate(tuned_as, "rearing")
r_rec_out <- rate(tuned_as, "accessible_not_rearing")
r_dflt_in <- rate("default", "rearing")
r_dflt_out <- rate("default", "accessible_not_rearing")
# "chinook are caught more often on the recommended rule's habitat, and less often off it, than on link's"
stopifnot(r_rec_in > r_dflt_in, r_rec_out < r_dflt_out)

# the stricter bar: the same choice from rules within se_strict standard errors (inst/method/settings.csv)
se_strict <- 1.96  # the register's se_strict
tune$in_196 <- tune$converged %in% TRUE & tune$ddev_best <= se_strict * tune$se_diff
ch196 <- knw_tune_repick(tune, se_mult = se_strict)
lab_strict <- paste("only at", se_strict, "SE")
# at 1.96 the choice moves toward link's: it keeps link's slope limit, raises the flow floor and keeps the
# near-a-river allowance, so it departs from link's in fewer dials; link's rule stays out
stopifnot(ch196$rule != rec$rule, ch196$grad_max == dflt$grad_max, ch196$grad_max < rec$grad_max,
          ch196$size_min > rec$size_min, ch196$departures < rec$departures, ch196$exc_d %in% rec$exc_d,
          ch196$exc_q %in% rec$exc_q,
          ch196$n_region > nrow(region),
          ch196$rule != dflt$rule, !tune$in_196[tune$is_default], sum(tune$in_196) == ch196$n_region,
          all(tune$in_196[tune$in_region]))

# the close calls reach the top of the slope list
stopifnot(max(region$grad_max) == max(tune$grad_max))

boot_mad <- sum(tune$boot_rec_share[tune$size_var == "mad"])
boot_grad <- sum(tune$boot_rec_share[tune$grad_max == rec$grad_max])
stopifnot(boot_mad > 0.9, boot_grad < 0.5)

# the fitted chance of a catch by flow and distance to a river: about the same near the river whatever the flow,
# rising with flow ten kilometres away
sf_ <- x$surface
r_at <- function(s, dm) sf_$rate[sf_$size == s & sf_$dist_m == dm]
near <- sf_$rate[sf_$dist_m == min(sf_$dist_m)]
far <- sf_$rate[sf_$dist_m == 10000][order(sf_$size[sf_$dist_m == 10000])]
stopifnot(length(near) == length(unique(sf_$size)), max(near) / min(near) < 1.5, all(diff(far) > 0),
          max(far) / min(far) > 5, rec$exc_d %in% sf_$dist_m, meta$curve_ref$q == rec$exc_q)

# lines through wetlands: `wl` is the structure reported as tuned (the door, link's own test for them since 0.67.0);
# the comparison runs the others only on STRUCTURES=all (#112), so the article reads this one alone
wl <- x$wetland[x$wetland$as_tuned, ]
stopifnot(nrow(wl) == 1, wl$structure == "door", wl$km_tuned < wl$km_default, wl$grade_median_tuned > 0.2)
# "in the comparison, link's rule counts them by their size or by a near-a-river pair": the comparison's link rule
# carries its pair on wetland-flow lines only
stopifnot(grepl("@D[0-9]+ on wetland_flow$", all_row$default_rule))

# the Bulkley map's words: what changes is mostly the drops far from a river and the gains beside one; the rest is
# both the other limits (the rules' predicates differ) and the spawning-connection step (the predicates agree)
bk <- as.data.frame(seg)[c("accessible", "flag_default", "flag_tuned", "pre_default", "pre_tuned", "mad", "dist_m",
                           "length_metre")]
bk <- bk[bk$accessible %in% TRUE & bk$flag_default != bk$flag_tuned, ]
below <- is.na(bk$mad) | bk$mad < rec$size_min
near_gain <- bk$pre_tuned & !bk$pre_default & below & !is.na(bk$dist_m) & bk$dist_m <= rec$exc_d
far_drop <- bk$pre_default & !bk$pre_tuned & below & (is.na(bk$dist_m) | bk$dist_m > rec$exc_d)
other_dial <- bk$pre_default != bk$pre_tuned & !near_gain & !far_drop
connect <- bk$pre_default == bk$pre_tuned
km_of <- function(i) sum(bk$length_metre[i])
stopifnot(km_of(far_drop) > km_of(!bk$flag_tuned) / 2, km_of(near_gain) > km_of(bk$flag_tuned) / 2,
          km_of(other_dial) > 0, km_of(connect) > 0)

link_site <- "https://www.newgraphenvironment.com/link/"
link_default <- sprintf("https://github.com/NewGraphEnvironment/link/tree/%s/inst/extdata/configs/default", meta$link_sha)
bfp <- "https://github.com/smnorris/bcfishpass/blob/3bd2824c300c5f9c0c041380d412a52987df1ebb"
```

Young chinook salmon do not always rear where they hatched: from earlier fish inventories in Alaska, Kirsch et al.
recommend looking for more chinook rearing in the lower reaches of small tributaries, other than the ones they
hatched in, of large rivers that hold chinook [-@kirsch_etal2014Fishinventory, p. 42]. British Columbia's electrofishing records point the same way, putting young
chinook in more of the province's small streams near large rivers, and in fewer far from one, than link's current fish
habitat definition allows. [`link`](`r link_site`) [@link] is an R package that maps where each
fish species can reach and where it can spawn and rear on BC's streams. Its standard settings,
[`default`](`r link_default`), start from the thresholds New Graph runs bcfishpass with
[@norris2024smnorrisbcfishpass]: for chinook rearing, `r words(dflt)`. The records support **`r words(rec)`**.
[How the tuning works](tuning-method.html) says [what a habitat definition is](tuning-method.html#thresholds), and
how one is tested and tuned.

```{r map-static, eval = !on_site, fig.width = 6, fig.height = map_h, out.width = "80%", fig.cap = paste0("Chinook rearing in the Bulkley watershed group (", meta$map_group, "), around Smithers, under each habitat definition. Orange: link's current habitat definition only (the legend's 'lost'). Green: the recommended habitat definition only (the legend's 'tuned only'). Blue: both. Line width follows stream order. The inset places the group in British Columbia.")}
f1 <- tempfile(fileext = ".png")
# no basemap here: this copy is built without network (R CMD check); the website's map has Esri's topographic map
knw_compare_map(seg, water, png = f1, panels = "rules", width = 6, scalebar = TRUE,
                keymap = list(aoi = ctx$aoi, context = ctx$bc), places = list(towns = ctx$towns, rivers = ctx$rivers),
                corners = c(legend = "topright", scalebar = "topleft", keymap = "bottomleft", logo = "bottomright"))
grid::grid.raster(png::readPNG(f1))
```

```{r map-site, eval = on_site, out.width = "100%"}
knw_compare_mapgl(seg, water, title = "Habitat definition", background = "esri_topo", scale = TRUE)
```

In the Bulkley watershed group, around Smithers, the recommended habitat definition draws `r n0(map_row$tuned_km)` km of rearing
habitat against `r n0(map_row$default_km)` under link's. What it drops (orange) is mostly the upper reaches of
tributaries, where flow falls below its floor more than `r km_d(rec$exc_d)` from a river. What it adds (green) is
short reaches of small streams beside a river. The rest comes from the two habitat definitions' own slope and flow
limits, and from link's step that keeps rearing only where it connects to spawning: that step keeps different stretches
under each.
`r if (on_site) "Click a stream for what each habitat definition reads there; the switch at the top right shows the grade, the use to expect on each segment." else ""`

## What changes?

The recommended habitat definition draws less habitat than link's, and chinook are caught on it more often and off it less often.

```{r changes}
cell_size <- function(r) {
  if (r$size_var == "mad") paste(format(r$size_min, trim = TRUE), "m³/s average flow")
  else paste(format(r$size_min, trim = TRUE), "m channel width")
}
cell_near <- function(r) {
  if (is.na(r$exc_q)) "none on stream lines" else paste0("smaller streams within ", km_d(r$exc_d), " of a ", r$exc_q, " m³/s river")
}
chg <- data.frame(
  ` ` = c("Smallest stream", "Steepest slope", "Near a river", "Rearing habitat",
          "Sites with chinook, on the habitat", "Sites with chinook, elsewhere"),
  `link now` = c(cell_size(dflt), grad(dflt$grad_max), cell_near(dflt), paste(n0(all_row$default_km), "km"),
                 pc(r_dflt_in), pc(r_dflt_out, 1)),
  `Recommended` = c(cell_size(rec), grad(rec$grad_max), cell_near(rec), paste(n0(all_row$tuned_km), "km"),
                    pc(r_rec_in), pc(r_rec_out, 1)),
  check.names = FALSE)
knitr::kable(chg, format = "html", align = "lrr",
             caption = "Chinook rearing under link's current habitat definition and the recommended one.") |>
  kableExtra::kable_styling(full_width = FALSE) |>
  kableExtra::footnote(general_title = "", general = paste0(
    "Habitat is summed over the ", nrow(per_group), " watershed groups link classified for chinook when the ",
    "comparison ran, each habitat definition run ",
    "through all of link's steps. Both totals include lines through wetlands, which the two habitat definitions test differently ",
    "(below). ",
    "Sites are the ", n0(sum(fv$n[fv$rule == "default"])), " electrofishing sites of a usual fished area on ",
    "reachable stream, river and wetland lines in those groups, a wider set than the one the habitat definition was chosen on. They overlap the sites it was chosen on, so the rates show it ",
    "does what it was chosen to do, not that it predicts new places."))
```

## Why does a nearby river matter?

Young chinook move up from large rivers into small streams close by. bcfishpass writes that idea with stream order:
where streams are sized by width, a first-order stream whose parent is order 5 or more counts as rearing below the
minimum width, if its width is mapped, along its whole length ([its chinook model](`r bfp`/model/02_habitat_linear/sql/load_habitat_linear_ch.sql)).
link's `default` leaves that exception off. A model fitted after the choice shows the same idea in the records, with a
distance on it:

```{r river, fig.height = 4, fig.cap = paste0("The fitted chance of catching chinook on one standard visit, by distance downstream to a river of at least ", meta$curve_ref$q, " m³/s, for four stream flows, at a slope of ", grad(meta$curve_ref$gradient), ". The dashed line is the recommended habitat definition's ", km_d(rec$exc_d), " allowance: beyond it, streams below its ", rec$size_min, " m³/s floor no longer count (grey). The fit is shown at six distances; the last stands for ", km_d(meta$curve_ref$dist_cap_m), " or more, or no such river, and is not joined.")}
rv <- sf_ |>
  mutate(flow = factor(format(size, trim = TRUE, drop0trailing = TRUE),
                       levels = format(sort(unique(size)), trim = TRUE, drop0trailing = TRUE)))
counted <- rv |> filter(size >= rec$size_min | dist_m <= rec$exc_d)
dropped <- rv |> filter(size < rec$size_min, dist_m >= rec$exc_d)
# the cap stands for "that far or more, or no such river", so it is drawn as a point, not joined to the curve
cap <- meta$curve_ref$dist_cap_m
stopifnot(max(rv$dist_m) == cap)
brk <- sort(unique(rv$dist_m))
lab <- vapply(brk, function(d) if (d >= meta$curve_ref$dist_cap_m) paste(km_d(d), "+") else km_d(d), "")
ggplot(rv, aes(dist_m, rate)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = rec$exc_d, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey40") +
  geom_line(data = filter(dropped, dist_m < cap), aes(group = flow), colour = "grey75", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(data = filter(dropped, dist_m == cap), colour = "grey75", size = 1.6) +
  geom_line(data = filter(counted, dist_m < cap), aes(colour = flow, group = flow), linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_point(data = counted, aes(colour = flow), size = 1.6) +
  scale_x_log10(breaks = brk, labels = lab) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = function(v) paste0(round(100 * v), " %")) +
  scale_colour_viridis_d(end = 0.85, direction = -1, name = "Stream flow (m³/s)") +
  labs(x = paste0("Distance downstream to a river of at least ", meta$curve_ref$q, " m³/s"),
       y = "Chance of catching chinook") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
```

Within `r km_d(min(sf_$dist_m))` of a river the chance is about the same whatever the stream's flow,
`r pc(min(near), 1)` to `r pc(max(near), 1)`. Ten kilometres away it rises with flow, from `r pc(min(far), 1)` to
`r pc(max(far), 1)`. That is the shape the recommended habitat definition draws: beside a river a small stream counts, away from one
only a larger stream does.

## How sure are we?

Scores carry error: another draw of watersheds would rank close habitat definitions differently. So the tuning
treats every habitat definition within one standard error of the best as a close call, a convention fixed before the run
([how two habitat definitions are told apart](tuning-method.html#se)). For chinook, `r nrow(region)` of `r n0(nrow(tune))`
habitat definitions are close calls, all with a flow floor of `r min(region$size_min)` to `r max(region$size_min)` m³/s, the
near-a-river allowance, and a slope limit of `r grad(min(region$grad_max))` or more. The tie-break fixed in advance
takes the close call nearest link's; all differ from link's on stream lines in every dial, so it is the best scorer.
link's habitat definition is
`r n1(dflt$ddev_best / dflt$se_diff)` standard errors behind it.

```{r profile, fig.height = 5.2, fig.cap = paste0("How close the best habitat definition using each value of each dial comes to the best overall, as score above the best (lower is better). Dark blue: at least one habitat definition with that value is a close call at one standard error; light blue: only at ", se_strict, " standard errors; white: neither. The orange ring marks the value of link's habitat definition on stream lines.")}
dial <- function(lab, v, key) {
  tune |>
    mutate(value = v) |>
    group_by(value, key = key) |>
    summarise(best = min(ddev_best), one = any(in_region), strict = any(in_196), .groups = "drop") |>
    mutate(part = lab)
}
size_lab <- paste(ifelse(tune$size_var == "mad", "flow", "width"), as.character(tune$size_min))
size_key <- ifelse(tune$size_var == "mad", tune$size_min, 10 + tune$size_min)
prof <- bind_rows(
  dial("Smallest stream (flow m³/s or width m)", size_lab, size_key),
  dial("Steepest slope", grad(tune$grad_max), tune$grad_max),
  dial("Near-a-river allowance: river size (m³/s)", ifelse(is.na(tune$exc_q), "none", format(tune$exc_q, trim = TRUE)),
       ifelse(is.na(tune$exc_q), -1, tune$exc_q)),
  dial("Near-a-river allowance: distance (m)",
       ifelse(is.na(tune$exc_d), "none", format(tune$exc_d, big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE)),
       ifelse(is.na(tune$exc_d), -1, tune$exc_d))
)
prof$part <- factor(prof$part, levels = unique(prof$part))
prof <- prof |>
  group_by(part) |>
  mutate(value = factor(value, levels = unique(value[order(key)]))) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(close = factor(ifelse(one, "close call at one SE", ifelse(strict, lab_strict, "neither")),
                        levels = c("close call at one SE", lab_strict, "neither")))
dflt_vals <- tibble::tibble(
  part = factor(levels(prof$part), levels = levels(prof$part)),
  value = c(paste("width", as.character(dflt$size_min)), grad(dflt$grad_max), "none", "none")
)
dpts <- inner_join(prof, dflt_vals, by = c("part", "value"))
stopifnot(nrow(dpts) == 4)
ggplot(prof, aes(value, best)) +
  geom_line(aes(group = 1), colour = "grey70") +
  geom_point(aes(fill = close), shape = 21, size = 2.6, colour = "grey20") +
  geom_point(data = dpts, shape = 21, size = 5, stroke = 1, colour = "#d95f02", fill = NA) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = stats::setNames(c("#1b6ca8", "#9ecae1", "white"), c("close call at one SE", lab_strict, "neither")),
                    drop = FALSE, name = NULL) +
  facet_wrap(~part, scales = "free_x", ncol = 2) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Score above the best") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1), legend.position = "bottom",
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
```

The flow floors near the best are close calls at one standard error and no width floor is; the slope limit is
flat from `r grad(min(region$grad_max))` up.

**A stricter bar.** At `r se_strict` standard errors, about the width of a 95 % interval, more habitat definitions are
close calls, and the choice moves toward link's. Of the close calls it takes the one that changes the fewest of
link's dials: it keeps link's slope limit of `r grad(ch196$grad_max)` and raises the flow floor from
`r rec$size_min` to `r ch196$size_min` m³/s, with the same near-a-river allowance:

```{r strict}
bold_if <- function(v, ref) ifelse(v != ref, paste0("<b>", v, "</b>"), v)
st <- data.frame(
  ` ` = c("Smallest stream", "Steepest slope", "Near a river"),
  `link now` = c(cell_size(dflt), grad(dflt$grad_max), cell_near(dflt)),
  check.names = FALSE)
st[["Chosen at 1 SE"]] <- bold_if(c(cell_size(rec), grad(rec$grad_max), cell_near(rec)), st[["link now"]])
st[[paste("Chosen at", se_strict, "SE")]] <-
  bold_if(c(cell_size(ch196), grad(ch196$grad_max), cell_near(ch196)), st[["link now"]])
knitr::kable(st, format = "html", escape = FALSE, align = "llll",
             caption = "The chinook rearing habitat definition chosen from the close calls at each bar, beside link's current one.") |>
  kableExtra::kable_styling(full_width = FALSE, font_size = 13) |>
  kableExtra::footnote(general_title = "", general = paste0(
    "Bold: differs from link's. Close calls: ", nrow(region), " habitat definitions at one standard error, ",
    n0(ch196$n_region), " at ", se_strict, "; link's is a close call at neither. This package's thresholds table (data/thresholds.csv, column ",
    "rule_196) gives the choice at ", se_strict, " for every species tuned."))
```

**Three other checks.**

```{r other-checks}
beats_all <- sum(honest$dev_rec) < sum(honest$dev_default)
oc <- data.frame(
  Check = c(paste(nrow(seeds), "other random splits into sets"),
            "Chosen on four sets, scored on the fifth",
            paste(meta$spec$n_boot, "redraws of the groups")),
  Result = c(paste0("the recommended habitat definition is a close call on ", sum(seeds$main_rec_in_region), " of ", nrow(seeds),
                    "; link's on ", sum(seeds$default_in_region)),
             paste0("the chosen habitat definition beats link's on ", sum(honest$dev_rec < honest$dev_default), " of ", nrow(honest),
                    " and ", if (beats_all) "beats it" else "loses to it", " overall"),
             paste0("a flow floor is chosen in ",
                    if (isTRUE(all.equal(boot_mad, 1))) "every draw" else paste(pc(boot_mad, 1), "of draws"),
                    "; the recommended slope limit in ", pc(boot_grad))),
  `Points to` = c(if (sum(seeds$main_rec_in_region) > sum(seeds$default_in_region)) "the recommended habitat definition" else "link's habitat definition",
                  if (beats_all) "choosing from the records" else "link's habitat definition",
                  "a steady shape; an unsettled slope limit"),
  check.names = FALSE)
knitr::kable(oc, format = "html", align = "lll") |>
  kableExtra::kable_styling(full_width = FALSE, font_size = 13)
```

## Before you use it

- **It is about young chinook in streams.** It was fitted to juvenile chinook caught by electrofishing in streams and
  says nothing about spawning. River polygons share the stream slope limit, so they get `r grad(rec$grad_max)` too,
  though no site in one was scored. Lines drawn through wetlands of 1 ha or more were tested by neither habitat
  definition's records. In the comparison, link's counts them by their size or by a near-a-river pair, and the
  recommended one puts them through the same test as a stream line, which leaves about
  `r n0(round(wl$km_tuned, -2))` km of them as chinook rearing under the recommended habitat definition, with a median grade of
  `r formatC(wl$grade_median_tuned, format = "f", digits = 2)`, against `r n0(round(wl$km_default, -2))` km under
  link's. Lakes keep their own condition.
- **The cut-offs are a judgment call.** Chinook get gradually less common as streams get smaller and steeper; there is
  no flow or slope where they stop. At one standard error, flow floors of `r min(region$size_min)` to
  `r max(region$size_min)` m³/s fit almost as well. At `r se_strict` standard errors the choice keeps link's slope limit
  of `r grad(ch196$grad_max)` and raises the flow floor from `r rec$size_min` to `r ch196$size_min` m³/s.
- **Steeper slopes fit nearly as well.** The close calls run from `r grad(min(region$grad_max))` to
  `r grad(max(region$grad_max))`, the top of the list, and `r grad(rec$grad_max)` is the best scorer among them, not a
  slope at which chinook stop.
- **It was not tested against bcfishpass's own exception.** The candidates never included the stream-order exception above,
  so the records show that the flow-and-distance allowance beats link's `default`, not that it beats bcfishpass's.
- **On the map, distance is measured from the bottom of each segment.** To choose the habitat definition, the distance to a river's
  bank was measured from each site. On the map it is measured from each segment's downstream end, so when that end is
  within `r km_d(rec$exc_d)` of the river the whole segment counts.

## How was this done?

| Step | For chinook rearing |
|:--|:--------|
| Records | The Fisheries Data Information System's electrofishing sites [@provinceofbritishcolumbia2022FisheriesData]: where crews fished, and whether they caught chinook. `r n0(summ$visits_in)` sites in `r summ$groups` watershed groups: those on ordinary stream lines, of a usual fished area, with no code in the catch that could hide chinook and no barrier to chinook downstream, in groups where link expected chinook when the tuning ran; the tests use the `r summ$groups_both` groups where chinook were caught at some sites and not others, **`r n0(dflt$n_visits)` sites, `r n0(dflt$n_detect)` with chinook**. ([More](tuning-method.html#steps)) |
| Placement | Each site went onto the BC Freshwater Atlas, loaded by fwapg [@norris2024smnorrisfwapg]. A site whose 1:50k tributary code the Atlas's crosswalk knows went to the nearest stream that code names, kept when it lay within 500 m of the point, and was dropped otherwise; a site with no such code went to the nearest stream, kept when it lay within 200 m. ([More](tuning-method.html#snap)) |
| Flow | wet's modelled average flow [@wet]: PCIC's VIC-GL runoff [@schnorbus2018VICGlacierVICGL] routed with Raven [@craig_etal2020Flexiblewatershed] and carried onto Atlas streams by a crosswalk in New Graph's fork of fwapg [@norris_irvine2026NewGraphEnvironmentfwapg], with wet's own water balance where that flow does not reach or, on a stream's own line, carries under a fifth of the balance's. |
| Slope | The slope of the segment a site sits on, on link's minimal network, which does not cut streams at sites that caught fish, so a site's slope hardly depends on its catch. ([More](tuning-method.html#cuts)) |
| Candidates | `r n0(nrow(tune))` habitat definitions, link's among them, from three dials: the smallest stream (an average flow of `r lst(sort(unique(tune$size_min[tune$size_var == "mad"])), "or")` m³/s, or a channel width of `r lst(sort(unique(tune$size_min[tune$size_var == "width"])), "or")` m); the steepest slope (`r lst(grad(sort(unique(tune$grad_max))), "or")`); and a near-a-river allowance (none, or a river of `r lst(sort(unique(na.omit(tune$exc_q))), "or")` m³/s within `r lst(format(sort(unique(na.omit(tune$exc_d))), big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE), "or")` m downstream). |
| Scoring | The groups were split into `r meta$spec$folds` sets, and each set was predicted by a model fitted to the others. The score adds up how far each prediction was from what the crew found; lower is better. ([More](tuning-method.html#se)) |
| Run by | fresh [@fresh], through all of link's steps for the map and the habitat totals. |
| Left out | The province's other fish observations, gathered in bcfishobs [@norris2024smnorrisbcfishobs]: they record where fish were found, not where they were sought and missed. Sites off ordinary stream lines, of an unusual fished area, with a code in the catch that could hide chinook, or with a barrier to chinook downstream. ([More](tuning-method.html#lost)) |

Table: How the chinook rearing habitat definition was tested.
